title: Equality as a relation: congruence axioms and quotient models
summary: Replace logical equality by a new relation, add five congruence schemes, and recover an ordinary model by taking equivalence classes.
abstract: Two different names can denote the same object, but an arbitrary binary relation cannot simply be used as equality. It must be an equivalence relation, and functions and predicates must respect the identifications it makes. We express these requirements as equality-free axioms and show that they are sufficient: collapsing related objects gives an ordinary structure in which every translated formula has exactly its original truth value. The argument covers quantifiers as well as atomic formulas. Consequently any first-order theory can have its equality replaced by one fixed new relation without changing whether it has a nonempty model. Writing the axioms as signed clauses makes this reduction available to equality-free clause methods.
